title: Universal Print: audit records in the Microsoft Purview unified audit log
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the Microsoft documentation checked. Its audit search controls, permissions, licensing and 180-day Universal Print retention default are supported; the remaining feature-specific documentation gaps were independently searched.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching the audit log in Purview requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Restricted administrators assigned administrative units can search and export only user-generated logs within their units.
claims.quote: A restricted admin can only search and export user-generated audit logs within the scope of their assigned administrative units.

claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can access all audit logs.

claims.claim: Audit search results show the user account that performed the activity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The current default audit retention for users with non-E5 Office 365 or Microsoft 365 licences is 180 days.
claims.quote: For users assigned any other (non-E5) Office 365 or Microsoft 365 license, the system retains audit records for 180 days.

claims.claim: E5 users receive one-year default retention for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange and SharePoint activity.
claims.quote: the system retains audit records for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, and SharePoint activity for one year by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Retention longer than 180 days and up to one year requires Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Purview Suite or E5 eDiscovery and Audit for the user generating the record.
claims.quote: the user who generates the audit log (by performing an audited activity) must have an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license or a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: An audit retention policy is needed to retain activities in services outside the one-year defaults for up to one year.
claims.quote: Organizations can also create audit log retention policies to retain audit records for activities in other services for up to one year.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Universal Print audit records fall outside the one-year workload defaults and have 180-day default retention unless a custom policy changes the duration.
claims.quote: AzureActiveDirectory, Exchange, OneDrive, and SharePoint for the Workload property ... Audit records for all other activities are retained for 180 days by default or you can change the retention to a different duration using a custom retention policy.

claims.claim: Auditing is not enabled by default for SMB licences including Business Premium.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Unified auditing must be on to search records; when it is off, Purview searches and Search-UnifiedAuditLog return no results.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results. Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: The Office 365 Management Activity API cannot access audit data when auditing is off.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft Sentinel cannot access audit data when auditing is off.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches audit search.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables unified auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
